title: Delhi High Court: Long Residence Abroad Does Not Bar an NRI Co-Owner's Right to Use Ancestral Property
case_name: Deepak Tara v. Baij Nath Tara
card_summary: A Swedish citizen in his mid-seventies, claiming a one-seventh share in an undivided ancestral property, sought relief against being kept out of a ground-floor room while his partition suit stayed pending. The Court allowed him access, holding long residence abroad does not extinguish a co-owner's rights, but confined the order to him and his immediate family during his Delhi stays, barring any third-party occupant.
card_tip: An NRI co-owner locked out of a joint family property by resident relatives can seek interim access during a pending partition suit without that access deciding anyone's final share in the property.
verification_notes: The Swedish citizenship and one-seventh share claim, the 2019 status quo order, the 23 January 2026 interim order in CS(OS) 73/2019 before Justice Subramonium Prasad, and the safeguards against third-party occupation are corroborated across Rawlaw's and Lawyer E News's reports, with the Delhi High Court's own order file (SMP23012026S732019) matching the case number and date.
